contract: S0 same-distribution main protocol (freeze candidate). Within each frozen parameter combo, independent repeats only; train/validation/test all cover the same beta x gamma x n grid. P = parameter-precision loss, Q = target x0.95 reliability-lifetime loss (see x_p_definition: R(x_p)=p, NOT a CDF p-quantile); per-fit paired, only loss route differs. RQ/estimand/inference/matrix in 09-PQ-同分布主协议冻结.md. r4/v3 (gamma/eta-level holdout) retained verbatim as OOD supplement only, not main evidence. R1 REVISE (2026-08-07): S0-001 x_p definition; S0-002 estimand/estimator consistency; S0-003 alignment scope; S0-004 strict protocol validation; cost basis corrected.
run_mode: PQ_PROTOCOL=iid-v1 (config.py env selector; default stays v3; unknown values rejected with ValueError)

identical_to_study01: parameter grid (beta, eta, gamma/eta, n, 300 repeats, 160 combos, 48000 samples)
sample generator contract generate_sample(..., seed=study01_nrmc_v1), namespace, sample key
raw ascending-sorted input representation; per-position StandardScaler fit on train rows only
main budget: max 300 epochs, patience 20, batch 256, lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4, train seeds 42/2026/3407
deliberately_different_from_study01: research label/loss: P and Q routes (Study01 has no such contrast; these are the study labels)
split purpose and scheme: Study01/sklearn uses gamma/eta-level holdout (OOD); this main protocol uses repeat-stratified 5-fold (same-distribution independent repeats)
optimizer implementation: Study01 sklearn trajectory; this protocol PyTorch Adam trajectory
alignment_scope.horizontal_analysis_scope: cross-study comparison only on shared sample identity (same grid, generator, input) AND comparable metric (both estimate the x_p reliability lifetime); does not assert equivalence of optimizer trajectories or split scheme

x_p_definition.meaning: x_p is the RELIABILITY LIFETIME satisfying the survival function R(x_p)=P(X>x_p)=exp(-((x_p-gamma)/eta)^beta)=p; equivalently the CDF (1-p) quantile. It is NOT the usual CDF p-quantile (which would use -ln(1-p)).
x_p_definition.m3_meaning: M3 levels 0.90/0.95/0.99 are RELIABILITY levels (survival probabilities), not CDF probabilities

split.rule: test: repeat_id % 5 == fold_idx; val: repeat_id % 5 == (fold_idx+1) % 5; train: remainder. Independent of seed and route.

validation.type: repeat class (fold+1)%5; deterministic; seed/route independent; NOT a random fraction

losses.Q: relative x0.95 (reliability lifetime R(x)=0.95) squared error through Weibull formula

training.x0p95: x_p = gamma + eta * (-ln p)^(1/beta), p=0.95; x_p satisfies survival R(x_p)=p (see x_p_definition), i.e. CDF (1-p) quantile, NOT the CDF p-quantile
training.support_legality: strict 0 < gamma_hat < min(X) structurally (domain-explicit bounded decoder; relies on frozen positive-gamma domain gamma in [100,1000], min(X)>gamma)
training.no_aux: no log-gap, no auxiliary gamma loss, no straight-through gradient, no route-specific init or decoder

estimated_wall_clock_min.basis: r4 120 fits = 1522 s total (mean 12.7 s/fit) on hermes venv torch 2.12.0+cpu single-thread; r4 optimizer-train rows = 8160 (dev 9600 then internal val split 0.15 -> 9600*0.85); iid optimizer-train rows = 7200 (val is a separate repeat class, not carved from train); ratio 7200/8160 ~ 0.88 -> ~11.2 s/fit typical, M1 ~22 min (15-30 depending on early stopping)

inference.estimand: Scientific target Delta* = equal-weight mean over the frozen parameter domain (each n, each cell within n) of E[theta_Q(c) - theta_P(c)], where the expectation is over independent fresh held-out repeated samples AND training randomness (weight-init seed, batch order, optimizer trajectory) under the frozen 180/60/60 training protocol. Delta* is a superpopulation-style algorithmic performance gap, NOT a property of the realized fold/seed grid.
inference.finite_estimate: The realized 5 folds x 3 seeds x 4 n grid gives d_{n,f,s} (equal-weight mean over 2400 held-out paired samples) and hat_Delta = equal-weight mean over the 60 model-level contrasts. This is a finite Monte Carlo / CV estimate of Delta*: folds are finite replicate draws of the train/test repeat split, seeds are finite draws of training randomness.
inference.primary: (n, fold) design-unit x seed crossed paired resampling (folds stratified by n with replacement, seeds resampled globally with replacement); B = 200000 for the reported CI, 2000 for smoke/tests
inference.uncertainty_interpretation: The crossed fold-x-seed bootstrap is a DESIGN-LEVEL empirical uncertainty approximation of hat_Delta as an estimate of Delta* (variability over which fold/seed realization occurred). Coverage caveats: (a) overlapping training folds (each repeat is train in 3 of 5 folds), (b) only 3 seeds, (c) within-unit per-sample MC noise is absorbed (only the unit mean is resampled). Per-sample bootstrap under fixed models remains a conditional supplement only.
inference.weighting_note: Under the fully balanced design every model has the same 2400 held-out samples and every cell the same 60 repeats, so Delta (hat_Delta) equals the pooled per-sample mean difference in rel_sq with identical weighting; rel_change differs from Delta by functional form (ratio of RMS vs linear difference in rel_sq), not by weighting. Both are reported with explicit denominators.
inference.secondary: per-sample bootstrap under fixed models (Monte Carlo interval only, conditional on trained models)
